# Mermaid's lazy chunks still register into Monaco's loader at first render

## Context

Successor to **#18564**, which #18565 resolved and which must stay closed — a ticket resolved by a merged PR is a record, and reopening it makes the `Resolves` linkage ambiguous. #18564's fix was correct and incomplete: it removed the collision at **library load** and left it at **first render**.

@neo-opus-grace found the remainder on merged `dev` and I reproduced it independently before accepting.

```
route: learn/tutorials/DockLayoutsFirstLayout   at dev@87e3786673
containers: 2 | svg: 0 | define.amd: true | livePreviews: 2
[error] Can only have one anonymous define call per script file
        at …/chunks/mermaid.esm.min/chunk-DZP67EKU.mjs:6:203
```

## The Problem

`mermaid.esm.min.mjs` is a 30 KB entry that lazily imports from `dist/chunks/mermaid.esm.min/` — 206 chunks. The **entry** carries no `define`, which is why #18565's switch made `loadFiles()` and `initialize()` succeed. Ten chunks still do, so the anonymous `define` lands in Monaco's loader at the moment a diagram first renders.

| measure | value |
|---|---|
| `.mjs` files under `mermaid/dist` | 274 |
| files containing `typeof define` | **10** |
| `define(` call sites | **26** |
| of those, guarded by `define.amd` | 22 |

⚠️ **The `.amd` guard does not protect us, and that is the counter-intuitive part.** Monaco's `define` *has* `.amd`, so `typeof define=="function"&&define.amd` takes the AMD branch exactly like the unguarded wrappers do. All 26 sites are hazards under Monaco. Two of them are vendored **`fastdom`**, not mermaid's own code, and check only `typeof define == "function"`.

**Why #18565's arm went green.** `LearnMermaidRender.spec.mjs` drives `guides/uibuildingblocks/DockLayouts`, which has **zero** live-preview fences. @neo-opus-grace's diagnosis is the general form and it corrects that arm's AC-2 directly:

> The precondition asserts the loader is **present**. The defect needs the loader to be **busy**.

`define.amd === true` on **both** routes, because the portal installs the loader app-wide — so the precondition passes everywhere and separates nothing. Monaco only has an anonymous `define` in flight where live previews instantiate editors.

| route | mermaid fences | live-preview fences | `define.amd` | with SVG |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `guides/uibuildingblocks/DockLayouts` | 2 | **0** | `true` | **4/4** ✅ |
| `tutorials/DockLayoutsFirstLayout` | 1 | **3** | `true` | **0/2** ❌ |

Same session, same tab, failing route re-tested immediately after the passing one — so not a poisoned loader, not a cache, not the diagram type.

## The Architectural Reality

Two approaches are already falsified, before anyone spends a cycle on them:

- **Hiding `window.define` around the render.** Chunks load asynchronously and, on exactly the routes that break, Monaco is *concurrently* loading modules. Hiding `define` trades a mermaid failure for a Monaco one.
- **Rewriting the identifier** (`define` → an undefined name). It breaks the `typeof define && define.amd` form: `typeof X` yields the truthy string `"undefined"`, and the right-hand `X.amd` then throws a `ReferenceError`. A rewrite that neutralises one guard form detonates another.

**What works — verified end to end, not reasoned.** A module-scope shadow prepended to each affected chunk:

```js
const define={amd:!1};
```

| guard form present in dist | with the shadow |
|---|---|
| `typeof define=="function"` | `"object"=="function"` → false |
| `typeof define && define.amd` | `"object" && false` → false |
| `(typeof define)[0]=="f"` | `"o"=="f"` → false |

Every form takes the non-AMD branch and none throws. No affected file declares `define` already (`grep -c 'const define\|let define\|var define\|function define'` → 0), and an ES module's top-level binding is file-scoped, so the shadow cannot leak.

**Proof**, patching one chunk locally on the failing route and reverting byte-identical afterwards:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| containers | 2 | 2 |
| **with SVG** | **0** | **2** |
| console error | anonymous-define | **none** |

## The Fix

A build step that copies `node_modules/mermaid/dist/` into `dist/mermaid/` and prepends the shadow to the affected files in transit, with `main.addon.Mermaid#mermaidPath` pointed at the built artifact.

It also closes a second, latent defect recorded on #18564's Out of Scope: **`dist/` contains no mermaid and no build script copies one**, so today's `node_modules` path is unreachable in a real deployment. One artifact answers both.

**Not the `build-highlightjs` shape.** I proposed that precedent before reading it: `buildScripts/build/highlightJs.mjs` *clones the upstream repository* and builds from source. For mermaid's 206-chunk esbuild output that is disproportionate — copy-and-transform is the smaller correct thing, and it keeps the pinned npm version as the single source of truth.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1 — a diagram renders on a route where Monaco is BUSY.** Verified on a live-preview route, not merely a loader-present one. This is the whole ticket; `guides/…/DockLayouts` already passes today and re-proving it is not evidence.
- [ ] **AC-2 — the arm's precondition discriminates.** ⚠️ `define.amd === true` is true on the passing and failing routes alike and separates nothing. The precondition must assert the condition the defect needs — an instantiated live preview / editor — or the arm repeats #18565's mistake with a new coordinate.
- [ ] **AC-3 — red-first against THIS defect.** At `dev@87e3786673` the tutorial route is red and the guide route green, so a correct arm distinguishes them *before* any fix lands. Both directions on the same arm.
- [ ] **AC-4 — every affected chunk is covered, not the one this reproduction happened to load.** `chunk-DZP67EKU.mjs` sufficed for this route; `ganttDiagram-*`, `architectureDiagram-*`, `cose-bilkent-*` and the non-min `mermaid.esm/` twins all carry wrappers, and other diagram types load them. The transform is driven by a **scan**, never a filename list.
- [ ] **AC-5 — the transform fails loudly on an upstream change.** If a future mermaid version introduces a guard form the shadow does not satisfy, or a file that already declares `define`, the build refuses rather than emitting a silently broken artifact.
- [ ] **AC-6 — `dist/` reachability.** A diagram renders in a built environment where `node_modules` is not part of the deployed tree.

## Out of Scope

- **#18548's author-runnable verification path** — the documented render-check with a deliberate-syntax-error control, plus the `guide-authoring` §3 corrections that span `neo-agent-skills`. This unblocks it further; it does not claim it.
- **The portal instantiating guide content twice.** Measured in passing on both routes — 2 containers for 1 fence, identical `textContent` length. Pre-existing, unrelated, and it is why container counts read double.
- **Patching `node_modules` at install time** (`postinstall`, `patch-package`). It would fix the dev path and leave `dist/` unreachable, i.e. solve the smaller half of the problem and hide the larger one.

## Avoided Traps

- **Sampling instead of polling.** The first measurement after the patch read `svg: 1` of 2 and I nearly filed a partial fix. Mermaid renders per-container asynchronously; the settled state is 2/2. This bit me twice today on the same surface.
- **Asserting the container.** #18548 names it: the container is emitted from the fence alone and is present throughout the outage.
- **Trusting a `.amd` guard.** 22 of 26 sites have one and every one of them still fires under Monaco.

## Decision Record impact

`none`. A build artifact and a path change; no runtime contract moves.

- #18548 — the verification-path ticket this unblocks further

## Why it used to work — the causal chain, and one alternative fix it rules out

@tobiu: *"before the builds change, mermaids rendered fine inside the portal app."* Chased it, because "it used to work" is the datum that most often relocates a fix.

**It is not a dependency bump.** `mermaid` is declared `^11.17.2` and has not moved since `047f56bac9` (2026-01-07); `11.17.2` is installed. The library is the same one that used to render.

**What changed is when Monaco's AMD loader becomes live:**

| step | evidence | confidence |
|---|---|---|
| `useLazyLoading` defaults to `false` | `src/main/addon/Base.mjs:47` | verified |
| `MonacoEditor` does not override it, and the portal lists it in `mainThreadAddons` | `apps/portal/neo-config.json:20` | verified |
| ⇒ its `loadFiles()` runs at app boot, so the loader is installed **app-wide**, not per-route | `define.amd === true` measured on both the passing and failing routes | verified |
| `ffd860b664` (#18355) made that load **actually complete** | before: `window.require = {paths: {vs: path}}` assigned directly. after: awaits the AMD factory and throws `Monaco AMD loader failed` on error. Its own added docblock: *"Loading editor.main.js as a script only registers its module; addon readiness requires the AMD factory to finish."* | ⚠️ **inferred from the diff, NOT measured on the parent commit** |

The last row is the one that explains the observation — before #18355 the AMD entry did not finish, so no live `define` sat on the page and mermaid's UMD bundle took its global branch. I have not run the parent commit to confirm it, and it is marked accordingly rather than asserted.

## The alternative this rules out

The obvious cheaper fix, given the chain above, is **`useLazyLoading: true` on `MonacoEditor`** — install the AMD loader only when an editor is actually needed. It does not work:

- it fixes `guides/uibuildingblocks/DockLayouts`, which **already renders 4/4** today, and
- it does not fix `tutorials/DockLayoutsFirstLayout`, because that route *instantiates live previews* — Monaco loads there by definition, which is the whole reason it is the failing route.

Making the load lazy also makes the collision **order-dependent** rather than absent: on a live-preview route it becomes a race between the first diagram render and the first editor instantiation. Trading a deterministic failure for a racy one is worse than leaving it.

⇒ The chunk transform in **The Fix** stands unchanged.

## AC-4 scan result, so the transform is not written against a filename list

`grep -rl 'typeof define\|define(' node_modules/mermaid/dist --include='*.mjs'` — **10 files**, in matched min/non-min pairs:

```
chunks/mermaid.esm.min/{architectureDiagram-2PNWDENW, chunk-DZP67EKU, chunk-H7VHZCWX, cose-bilkent-Q72C2OJ3, ganttDiagram-RWFTB7ED}.mjs
chunks/mermaid.esm/{architectureDiagram-WKWPMKOY, chunk-LBQO3HYP, chunk-X5WJYYCX, cose-bilkent-4AQBBBIC, ganttDiagram-4PXIKP4L}.mjs
```

The pairing matters: `mermaidPath` points at the **min** entry today, but the non-min twins carry the same wrappers, so a transform scoped to one build silently leaves the other broken for anyone who repoints it.

**None of the 10 declares `define`** (`grep -cE '(const|let|var|function)[[:space:]]+define\b'` → 0 on every file), so the module-scope shadow cannot collide with an existing binding. That is the precondition AC-5 has to keep asserting on every future upstream version, not a one-time check.
